title: Data reduction and feature generation techniques for classification algorithms on heterogeneous behavioural data
authors: Gavric, M.; Zorko, M.; Slijepcevic, S.
tldr: Introduces an abstract semi-automated feature generation framework for classification on heterogeneous behavioral data that improves model accuracy 3-fold over fully automated approaches.
problem_and_motivation: Automated feature generation often results in model under-performance for business classification tasks involving time series and tabular data. Expert-knowledge-driven feature engineering is critical but lacks a scalable framework.
approach: Develops abstract data structure unifying event, customer segmentation, and outcome tables across use cases.
Semi-automated feature generation procedure incorporating expert knowledge via configurable statistics and parameters.
Six-step feature generation process: triggers segmentation, response aggregation, recency/frequency analysis, trend computation, segmentation interactions, and outcome alignment.
Validated on three production use cases: predicting engagement, propensity to buy, and behavioral credit scoring.
Deployed on AWS infrastructure using R, Apache Spark, and mlr3/tidymodels frameworks.
findings: num: Proposed feature generation improves model accuracy 3-fold or more vs automated-only approaches.
num: Feature generation contributes more to accuracy than model choice or parameter fine-tuning.
num: AUC range of 0.76-0.86 across three production use cases with 284 selected features from 26,637 generated.
Data leakage prevention requires both time-split and customer-split validation strategies.
Content labeling across channels is critical for engagement prediction use case.
Overdraft history, age, and transaction amount percentiles are top features for credit scoring.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides a formal abstract framework for feature generation on heterogeneous behavioral data combining time series and tabular sources. Demonstrates that expert-guided semi-automated feature engineering dramatically outperforms fully automated approaches. Validates framework across multiple production business use cases including credit scoring.
directly_justifies: Expert-guided feature generation improves accuracy 3-fold vs automated.
Feature generation contributes more to accuracy than model selection.
Abstract framework unifies engagement, purchase, and credit scoring use cases.
Time-split and customer-split validation prevents data leakage.
limits: Single company context may limit generalizability.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all domains. Assigned 5.C, 6.A, 12.B, 14.B high relevance for classification, prediction, evaluation, and deployment. Rejected demographic and mobile topics as paper focuses on ML framework.

limitations: Framework requires significant expert knowledge investment.
Production examples from single company context.
Scalability to very large datasets not thoroughly addressed.
